summary.name: The Ripple Effect Of Outages And Downtime
summary.one_liner: A sponsored article (part of a CDN performance series by Dyn) arguing that website outages cost businesses revenue, customer trust and loyalty, and that most outages are avoidable.
use_cases: Making the business case for outage prevention
Understanding the financial cost of downtime
Reviewing statistics on customer behaviour after outages
summary.what_it_does: The article describes how website and network outages affect a business beyond direct lost revenue, citing figures on lost revenue per hour of downtime, customer non-return rates, and customers switching to competitors. It attributes the largest cause of network outages to human error, citing Gartner and Dimension Data, and argues that customers blame the company rather than the Internet. It recommends internet performance management and continuity planning. It mentions Dyn's cloud service that monitors routes to and from cloud, CDN and datacenter locations, but gives no product details, pricing or technical specifics.
notable: Cites Apple's 11-hour outage in March 2015 and estimated costs of about US$163,000 per hour for successful businesses
Cites Gartner and Dimension Data figures that human error is the top cause of network outages, up to 32%
Promotes Dyn's cloud route-monitoring service as a sponsored piece
caveats: Sponsored content from Dyn, a vendor, so the product pitch is one-sided
Statistics are secondhand citations from older studies (2014-2016 era) and are not verified here
Describes the Dyn service only at a high level
